content: Junctional adhesion molecule B (JAM2) is a protein in humans encoded by the JAM2 gene. This protein is also referred to as CD322, which stands for cluster of differentiation 322. Tight junctions, where JAM2 is localized, are specialized structures that mediate cell-to-cell adhesion in endothelial cell sheets. These junctions form continuous seals around cells, acting as a physical barrier to restrict the free passage of solutes and water through the paracellular space. JAM2, as a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily, is specifically found in the tight junctions between high endothelial cells. JAM2 functions as an adhesive ligand, facilitating interactions with various immune cell types. It is believed to play a significant role in lymphocyte homing to secondary lymphoid organs. Additionally, JAM2 is thought to promote the transendothelial migration of lymphocytes, a critical step in immune surveillance and response. JAM2 may also contribute to the establishment and maintenance of endothelial cell polarity. This function is potentially mediated through its association with the cell polarity protein PAR-3, in conjunction with JAM3. In terms of molecular interactions, JAM2 has been demonstrated to interact with PARD3 (partitioning defective 3 homolog). Furthermore, it binds to the integrin dimer VLA-4, also known as α4β1 integrin, which is involved in cell adhesion and migration processes.
